summary: Preferred-edge fallback path selection causing intermittent inter-region egress and 120-200ms latency spikes
description: Issue summary: BrightForms (enterprise) reports intermittent 120-200ms latency spikes for requests pinned to eu-west. Traces show a subset of requests egressing to ap-south-1 for model execution, causing higher P95 for certain users. Customer has strict data residency configured with a preferred_edge set to eu-west but also uses a 'preferred_edge: ap-south-1' override for a small user cohort. Impact: Increased end-to-end latency for production traffic, user-facing perf regressions for EU customers. No data exfiltration reported but customer concerned about cross-region egress. Environment: Production clusters in eu-west (primary), ap-south-1 available as fallback capacity. Residency mode: strict (should not egress outside eu-west unless fallback). Routing policy version: v2.4.2 (recent deploy on 2026-03-09).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer creates requests with residency: strict and preferred_edge: eu-west.
2) Send 10k routine generation requests across their user pool with user_id hashes that map to affinity buckets.
3) Observe latency distribution and trace a sample of high-latency requests.
4) Confirm that some traces show egress hop to ap-south-1 even though eu-west had available capacity for the same model variant.
Notes: Issue is intermittent and correlates with autoscaler events and a recent routing-service rollout.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: routing v2.4.2 introduced a change to fallback ordering that weighed available capacity ahead of residency preference in corner cases.
What we checked: routing config for BrightForms account, node capacity snapshots, autoscaler roll logs, and full traces.
Findings:
- eu-west had transient capacity dip during rolling update; however capacity was available for most buckets.
- route-selection logic contains a capacity-first branch for 'preferred_edge' overrides; when preferred_edge exists, policy falls back to any region that satisfies model flavor and capacity without re-checking strict residency enforcement for that customer.
- affinity hashing caused ~6% of requests to map to buckets that hit the capacity-first code path during autoscaler churn.
- No auth/ACL violations observed; data access controls and encryption are intact.
Open questions:
- Is strict residency expected to block fallback to other regions entirely for enterprise customers, or only to prefer same-region first? Customer expected strict block unless explicit emergency fallback is allowed.
comments: Priya Rao (2026-03-10 12:05): Logged after initial customer call. Customer provided trace samples and stateful session IDs.

SRE - Daniel Kim (2026-03-10 14:30): Reproduced intermittent ap-south-1 egress in staging using the customer affinitized traffic pattern. Observed route-selection behavior that favors capacity when preferred_edge is mixed. Opening INT-4128 to track routing-service fix and rollback plan.

Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-11 09:12): Shared recommended immediate workaround with customer: enable 'strict_failover_block: true' on their account to prevent cross-region fallback while we investigate. Customer applied change and saw latency reduction for a 2-hour window.

Customer - BrightForms SRE (Luca Moretti) (2026-03-11 11:40): Confirmed strict_failover_block reduced cross-region egress but they need SLA-safe default behavior without manual toggles. Asked for timeline for a permanent fix.
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: instructed customer to toggle 'strict_failover_block: true' on their account (applied 2026-03-11 09:20). This prevents capacity-based cross-region fallback but can reduce burst capacity — communicated tradeoff.
Planned fix: Patch routing-service to re-enforce account-level residency checks before capacity-based fallback when residency=strict, and add unit + integration tests for preferred_edge + autoscaler churn scenarios. Patch: github PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/891 - target deploy to routing-service on 2026-03-14 with canary in eu-west-only first.
Postmortem action items:
- INT-4128: hotfix and deploy routing-policy change (owner: SRE).
- Add alert for 'preferred_edge fallback egress' spike to console dashboards.
- Update residency documentation to clarify strict vs preferred_edge semantics (owner: Product Docs).

customer_impacted_users_estimate: ~12% of active EU user sessions during peak windows showed elevated P95 due to these fallback paths
notes_for_engineering: Priority: high. Key issue is ordering in route selection algorithm where 'preferred_edge overrides + capacity-first fallback' can bypass strict residency enforcement for enterprise accounts. Suggested fix: short-circuit residency check for accounts with residency=strict before evaluating capacity-based fallback. Also add feature-flag to revert to old behavior quickly.
